answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with refundable epoch tickets: each agent locks a small deposit for one ticket per epoch, refunded only after peers attest its completed work. One honest agent can cover a whole voyage of tasks on a single ticket, so its cost per job is tiny, while an attacker must buy a fresh ticket for every fake identity and forfeits the deposit when its empty work is rejected. The velvet glove is that the ticket is refundable, so newcomers are not priced out — yet a Sybil summit flooding the network pays linearly more per identity than any gain from fake attestations.
